findings.title: raw_html cook_method bypasses all sanitization for externally sourced content
findings.body: Post#cook now returns `raw` unmodified when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, completely skipping PrettyText/post_analyzer rendering and sanitization. This path is used by TopicEmbed.import for content retrieved from RSS feeds and third-party web pages via Readability (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Since the content originates from an untrusted external source (a feed the admin configured, or any page fetched via the embed flow), and the resulting `cooked` HTML is rendered unescaped (`<%= raw post.cooked %>` in app/views/embed/best.html.erb and in normal topic views), a malicious or compromised feed/page can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript that executes in the context of the forum for every visitor who views that topic, not just inside the embed iframe. This is a stored XSS vector that defeats the forum's normal sanitization guarantees.

findings.title: Protocol-relative URLs are mangled by absolutize_urls
findings.body: `absolutize_urls` treats any href/src starting with '/' as a site-relative URL and rewrites it by stripping all leading slashes and prefixing with the embed site's scheme+host. Protocol-relative URLs such as `//cdn.example.com/x.jpg` also start with '/', so this code strips both leading slashes and produces `http://<embedhost>/cdn.example.com/x.jpg` instead of leaving the external URL `http://cdn.example.com/x.jpg` untouched. This breaks images/links that use protocol-relative URLs, which are common on syndicated content.

findings.title: postMessage origin check uses unsafe substring match
findings.body: `postMessageReceived` validates the sender using `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, i.e. it checks whether the message's origin string appears anywhere inside `discourseUrl`, rather than checking that `e.origin` equals (or is a prefix match of) the trusted Discourse origin. This is a well-known postMessage anti-pattern: a crafted or coincidental origin that happens to be a substring of `discourseUrl` (e.g. a shared domain fragment) could pass this check and have its `discourse-resize` messages accepted, allowing an untrusted page to manipulate the iframe height from outside the embed context.

findings.title: Referer host comparison is case-sensitive
findings.body: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host` compares hostnames with case-sensitive string equality. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so a referer like `Example.com` would fail to match a configured `embeddable_host` of `example.com` (or vice versa), causing legitimate embed requests to be incorrectly rejected with InvalidAccess.

findings.title: Potential NoMethodError when RSS/Atom item has no content
findings.body: `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes `i.content` is always present. Many RSS 2.0 feeds use `description` rather than `content`, and SimpleRSS will return `nil` for a missing `content` field, causing `.scrub` to raise `NoMethodError` on `nil` and aborting the whole feed-polling job (and since `sidekiq_options retry: false`, the failure is silently dropped) for every item that lacks a `content` element, not just the problematic one.

findings.title: feed_key is defined but never used
findings.body: `feed_key` computes a Redis cache key presumably meant to track the feed's last-modified state (to avoid reprocessing/refetching unchanged feeds), but it is never referenced anywhere in `poll_feed`. As written, the job always re-downloads and re-parses the entire feed and iterates every item on every run, with no last-modified/ETag based short-circuiting, making this dead code and a missed optimization opportunity.

findings.title: Full feed poll executed synchronously per missing embed request
findings.body: `perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline whenever an embed_url isn't found and feed polling is enabled, which downloads and parses the entire configured RSS/Atom feed and imports every item just to possibly locate the single requested embed_url. Because the throttle in `retrieved_recently?` is keyed per `embed_url`, concurrent requests for different not-yet-imported embed URLs each trigger their own full feed fetch/parse/import cycle with no global throttle, which can hammer the external feed URL and do redundant work under load (e.g. many visitors loading many different not-yet-cached embed pages at once).

findings.title: Core poll_feed RSS parsing/import logic is untested
findings.body: The spec only verifies that `execute` delegates to `poll_feed` under the right site-setting conditions, but it never exercises `poll_feed` itself: there is no coverage for RSS/Atom item iteration, URL fallback to `i.id`, HTML unescaping, or the call to `TopicEmbed.import`. Given this is the main new behavior introduced by this PR (feed-based topic creation/import), the lack of a test for `poll_feed`'s actual body is a significant gap.

findings.title: New gems only reflected in the Rails 4 lockfile
findings.body: The Gemfile adds `ruby-readability` and `simple-rss` unconditionally (outside the rails3/rails4 branch), but only `Gemfile_rails4.lock` is updated in this diff to include them. The repository supports dual-booting Rails 3 via a separate default `Gemfile.lock` (per the monkey-patching at the top of the Gemfile); if that lockfile isn't also updated, `bundle install`/`bundle exec` in Rails 3 mode will fail or be inconsistent with the new dependencies required by the embed/feed-import feature.
